Examples:
  nyx completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_nyx"
  nyx completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/nyx
  source <(nyx completion zsh)

completion prints a script to stdout that makes the shell complete nyx's commands, flags, help topics
and the values a flag takes from a fixed list: procedures, fields and record kinds. Save it where the shell
loads completions, or add source <(nyx completion bash) to ~/.bashrc, or source <(nyx completion zsh) to
~/.zshrc after compinit. bash needs the bash-completion package. The script asks nyx for its
completions, so it stays current when nyx is upgraded. To answer, nyx reads no file and contacts
nothing; file and directory names are completed by the shell.

Usage:
  nyx completion bash|zsh [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   Help for completion

Shared flags:
      --debug   Also write diagnostics to stderr: each failed job (recon), each request to the NVD (cve), each address probed (ip --active), and the stack of an unexpected failure
  -J, --json    Print the result as one JSON object on stdout, and any error as one JSON line on stderr
  -q, --quiet   Write only warnings and errors to stderr; recon's summary is still printed

Exit codes: 0 success, 1 system error, 2 usage error, 3 not found, 7 partial result, 130/143/129 interrupted (SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP)
